title: Intrinsic finite local models and fixed coefficient local models
statement: Let X be a scheme and R a commutative Noetherian ring. For the intrinsic module category and finitely presented local models of [def-sfb-proetale-fp-local-models], form the equivalence E obtained by restricting to constant scalars [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-encoding], transporting to the AsSmall equivalent site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and applying the inverse constant-ring module encoding [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves]. Then F has finitely presented constant local models if and only if E(F) is a finite type locally constant module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-locally-constant-module-sheaf] on the equivalent small site. The comparison identifies each local value M itself; it does not require points or finite underlying coefficient sets.

proof.text: On any localized site, restrict module sheaves along the constant-ring unit. This restriction is fully faithful: a map linear on constant sections is linear on arbitrary ring sections after a covering, because the unit is locally surjective. Equality of maps descends by the sheaf condition. Thus isomorphisms can be lifted through restriction.

Map the constant module presheaf to its intrinsic module sheafification. Adjunction extends the resulting fixed-scalar map to the constant module-valued sheaf. Its underlying additive map is locally bijective: both sheafification units are locally bijective and their composites agree on constants. Hence this map is an isomorphism. Apply the same construction on every slice, including empty objects. This identifies intrinsic constant local models with fixed-module-valued constant local models.

Transport to AsSmall using its up/down equivalence and induced topology. On slices use the corresponding Over.post equivalence. These transports take constant sheaves to constants by the constant sheaf adjunction and pull covering sieves to covering sieves. Applying the inverse transport gives the converse, with the same module M.

Apply the constant-ring restriction equivalence on the small site. Its counit identifies restriction of its inverse image with the given module-valued sheaf. The slice sheafification comparison from the second step identifies the local constants of this encoding with those used by the finite-type predicate. Over a Noetherian ring finite presentation implies finite generation and finite generation implies finite presentation. Transport the local isomorphisms and these finiteness properties in both directions.

theorem proEtale_fp_localModels_comparison (X : Scheme.{u}) (R : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (F : proEtaleRingModules X (proEtaleConstantRing X R)) :
    IsFinitelyPresentedLocallyConstantProEtaleModule F ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant (proEtaleModelTopology X)
        (ULift.{u + 1, u} R) ((proEtaleFPModelEncoding X R).functor.obj F)
